one-line thesis: Capacity expansion is largely complete with Wada plant ramping up, and sustainability initiatives (solar + recycling) are now operational, setting up margin expansion in H2FY26; the key shift is from capex-driven growth to utilization-driven profitability.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +21% YoY to ₹161cr; EBITDA: +21% YoY to ₹12.6cr (margin stable at 7.8% due to fixed cost ramp-up); PAT: +8% YoY to ₹6.2cr (normalized PAT higher by ~15% if excluding one-off Wada fixed cost inflation); order book: not disclosed; net debt: ₹140cr (short-term ₹66cr, long-term ₹74cr) with working capital pressure from capex funding
guidance: Revenue growth: 15% YoY for FY27; EBITDA margin: 11-12% by FY27; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: ₹15-20cr in FY27 for machinery expansion, no new greenfield
segment / subsidiary detail: MS Drum: volume +14% YoY, revenue +7% YoY (automation complete); HDPE Drum: volume +16% YoY, revenue +11% YoY; IBC: volume +42% YoY, revenue +30% YoY (export demand reviving post-tariff normalization)
growth verticals / optionality: New industrial packaging product line to be announced in next 1-2 quarters; potential capacity addition at existing Wada and Gujarat sites via machinery upgrades
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin improving due to recycling plant (10-12% raw material cost reduction) and solar (₹15cr annual power savings); EBITDA margin constrained in Q2 by ₹2cr+ fixed cost inflation (labor ₹83L, electricity ₹70L, depreciation ₹45L) at Wada; margin expansion of 800-900 bps expected from automation in MS drum segment
capex / expansion: ₹60cr completed in FY26 (Wada plant, solar, recycling); FY27 capex guidance: ₹15-20cr for machinery expansion only; no new land acquisition planned
capital allocation: Prioritizing debt repayment (EMIs start next quarter), reinvesting in automation and capacity utilization; no dividend policy mentioned; recycling and solar CAPEX funded via debt with 4-year payback
risks & watch-items: Tariff barriers impacting IBC exports; delayed GPCP certification for recycling plant; high working capital pressure from capex-funded growth; margin compression if volume growth stalls
management quality / tone: Confident and optimistic, emphasizing operational inflection point; management stresses 'now it's time to deliver' post-capex, with clear focus on utilization and margin expansion; tone is proactive on sustainability and automation
non-obvious takeaways: Recycling plant's ₹15cr annual savings are not yet reflected in P&L due to pending GPCP certification, creating a hidden upside; solar savings of ₹3-3.5cr in Q3 are already being realized despite delayed full commissioning

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Founded in 1997, described as "a prominent industrial packaging company known for our polymer-based molded products", specialising in rigid Intermediate Bulk Containers (IBCs), Polymer Drums and Mild Steel Drums used by the chemical, agrochemical, specialty chemical and pharmaceutical industries.
- Well-diversified client base: "Top Customer contributes 6% to revenues and top10 together accounts for 29%", across 500+ customers and 500+ workforce, with a fleet of 99 trucks and pan-India presence.
- Quality/compliance as a moat: IBCs and MS Drums carry UN certification conforming to IS 1783:2014, plus IIP (Govt of India) approval and international TUV certification of IBC from TUV Singapore; the deck also cites IBC collection services in the USA and Europe.
- Comprehensive portfolio positioned as "complete bulk industrial packaging solutions" - IBCs (1,000 L, four pallet types), plastic barrels/HDPE drums from 20 L to 250 L and higher, and MS drums of 200-210 L.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [FY27 guidance] The "Strategic Roadmap for FY27" sets an expected outcome of revenue growth ~15% and EBITDA margin ~11%-12%.
- [War impact] The deck repeatedly flags an external demand shock: "Near-term volume hit by the war; capacity and per-tn profitability unaffected" and "IBC volumes were specifically hit as export demand suffered due to the war", partly offset by MS Drums (+51% YoY) and IBC-Polymer (+7%).
- [Milestones] Journey slide: incorporation 1997, production of polymer drums at Silvassa 1998, IBC production at Bharuch, MS drums at Bharuch, Rs 400 Cr turnover in 2023, conversion to public limited, Wada operations commenced 2025, and solar power & recycling plant operations commenced 2026.
- [Promoter-led board] Leadership is family-led - Mr. Bijaykumar Agarwal (MD & Chairman, three decades in packaging), Mr. Jaiprakash Agarwal (WTD & CFO, 19 years) and Mrs. Madhu Agarwal (WTD).
